home.h1: Web development with WordPress, Next.js and a bias for speed
home.lead: I build sites and make them fast: custom WordPress plugins, WooCommerce stores at scale, and Next.js applications. Every project ships with a number you can check, not a feeling.
home.servicesLead: Six things I do well and do often.
home.workLead: Every case study starts with a problem and ends with a number you can see before and after.
home.blogLead: Things I learn on the job that are worth writing down.
home.approachLead: Three rules that keep projects finishing.

approach.title: Measure first
approach.body: Before touching code I record the current state: LCP, INP, CLS, transfer size, database queries. Without a baseline, "it got faster" is a claim, not a result.

approach.title: Smallest change, largest effect
approach.body: A full rewrite is usually the most expensive and least effective option. I find the actual bottleneck first — it is often a handful of bad queries, a 400 KB slider and one plugin loading on every page.

approach.title: Handover with documentation
approach.body: Code without explanation is technical debt. Every project ships with a short document: what changed, why, and where to look when you want to touch it later.

home.ctaBody: Send a short description. If I'm a fit I'll say so, if I'm not I'll say that too, and if I know someone better suited I'll point you to them.

about.title: About Ali Fatehi
about.description: Freelance web developer. WordPress at the core and hook level, Next.js and React, Python, and Core Web Vitals work.
about.lead: I'm Ali Fatehi, a freelance web developer.
body: I started with WordPress and a large part of my work is still WordPress — but not at the install-a-theme level. I work with core, hooks and filters, write custom plugins, and open WooCommerce up as far as needed to change how it behaves.

Alongside that I build with Next.js and React, front and back. I use Python for data work and automation, and I'm comfortable in MySQL and PostgreSQL — which in practice means that when a site is slow, I know the problem isn't always on the front end.

What interests me most is speed. Core Web Vitals aren't a decorative score; they're a direct measure of whether a visitor stays or leaves. That's why I record the before and after numbers on every project I take.

This site is deliberately built to be its own portfolio piece: no purchased theme, no unnecessary libraries, bilingual from the ground up with CSS logical properties, and a Lighthouse score you can run yourself right now.
